findings.claim: CompositeResolverTemplate (.tt and .cs) emits ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally, ignoring the new Options.Generator.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage opt-out, unlike every other template. README says opt-out is via GeneratedMessagePackResolver(ExcludeFromCodeCoverage=false), and this makes the opt-out incomplete for composite resolvers.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a CompositeResolver (via the [CompositeResolver] attribute) with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage=false and assert the output has no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute; it will fail. Also CompositeResolverTemplate.cs does not read Options at all.

findings.claim: The new test only asserts opt-out on a GeneratedMessagePackResolver and does not cover CompositeResolver output, so the unconditional emission is not caught. AllGeneratedTypes test also never exercises the composite resolver or generic formatters/nested types.

receipt_plan.detail: Remove the attribute line from CompositeResolverTemplate.tt/.cs; CodeCoverageExclusionTests still pass because no composite resolver is in TestSource.

findings.claim: The attribute is skipped on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework, so the requirement 'all generated code is decorated' is not met on those targets, though the guard is needed to compile. README documents it; the acceptance criterion allows conditional emission.

receipt_plan.detail: Requirement criterion 'attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted' permits the #if guard; no ledger entry. Noted as checked.

findings.claim: Adds a new public API property on GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute, a public surface expansion beyond the requirement that no setting is needed. PublicAPI.Unshipped is updated, but net6/other TFM files may be missing if any exist, and no docs under doc/ were added.

receipt_plan.detail: Check all src/MessagePack/*/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt directories; diff covers net472, net8.0, netstandard2.0, netstandard2.1 only.

findings.claim: The README attribution says 'opt out with GeneratedMessagePackResolver' but formatters for types are emitted per-assembly via the resolver attribute; if a project has no GeneratedMessagePackResolver, no opt-out is possible, and the option is read only from that attribute.

receipt_plan.detail: Read AnalyzerUtilities option parsing: generatorAttribute may be null for projects without the attribute; confirm default true is applied then.

questions.text: Should the opt-out setting exist at all, given the requester said a setting is not needed but would be fine?
options: Keep the opt-out property on GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute (public API addition)
Remove the setting and emit unconditionally
questions.why_it_matters: If unconditional is wanted, the new public API, option plumbing and opt-out test are unneeded scope; if the opt-out is kept, the CompositeResolver bypass becomes a real defect.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Attribute emitted by default on all generated types (formatters, resolvers, helper classes), with an opt-out property ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute and an #if guard for netstandard2.0/.NET Framework.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Unconditional emission with no setting: remove the new attribute property, GeneratorOptions.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, the AnalyzerUtilities parsing, PublicAPI entries and the template if-blocks; templates always emit the guarded attribute.
